title: Mixed commutator coefficient of infinitesimal matrix points
statement: Let k be a field, let V be a finite-dimensional k-vector space, and let G be a closed subgroup scheme of GL(V) [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Using the dual-number rings of [def-sc-dual-numbers], let A be the k-algebra k[\varepsilon,\delta]/(\varepsilon^2,\delta^2), with k-basis 1,\varepsilon,\delta,\varepsilon\delta. If X,Y\in\operatorname{End}_k(V) satisfy 1+\varepsilon X\in G(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2) and 1+\delta Y\in G(k[\delta]/\delta^2), then their base changes to A lie in G(A), and the commutator (1+\varepsilon X)(1+\delta Y)(1-\varepsilon X)(1-\delta Y) lies in G(A) and equals 1+\varepsilon\delta(XY-YX). The k-algebra map k[\eta]/(\eta^2)\hookrightarrow A given by \eta\mapsto\varepsilon\delta therefore shows 1+\eta(XY-YX)\in G(k[\eta]/\eta^2).

source.place: Chapter 10, differential of multiplication and commutator

proof.text: The maps k[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2) \to A and k[\delta]/(\delta^2) \to A sending the named nilpotent to \varepsilon and \delta are k-algebra maps. Hence the two given points base-change to elements of G(A) by functoriality of the defining equations. By [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], G(A) is a subgroup of GL(V\otimes_k A), so their product with the inverses 1-\varepsilon X and 1-\delta Y is again a G(A)-point.

source.place: Chapter 10, differential of multiplication and commutator

proof.text: Using \varepsilon^2=\delta^2=0 and centrality of the scalar nilpotents, direct multiplication gives (1+\varepsilon X)(1+\delta Y)(1-\varepsilon X)(1-\delta Y)=1+\varepsilon\delta(XY-YX): after the first two factors the terms are 1+\varepsilon X+\delta Y+\varepsilon\delta XY, multiplication by 1-\varepsilon X cancels the pure \varepsilon term and changes the mixed term to \varepsilon\delta(XY-YX), and multiplication by 1-\delta Y cancels the pure \delta term without changing that mixed term.

source.place: Chapter 10, differential of multiplication and commutator

proof.text: Let Z=XY-YX. The displayed matrix is therefore 1+\varepsilon\delta Z and is a G(A)-point. To descend this membership, write each defining equation of the closed subgroup G as a polynomial in the matrix entries. Evaluating it at 1+\varepsilon\delta Z has the form c+\varepsilon\delta d, while evaluating at 1+\eta Z in k[\eta]/(\eta^2) has the same coefficients c and d with \eta in place of \varepsilon\delta. Since 1,\varepsilon,\delta,\varepsilon\delta are k-linearly independent in A, the vanishing in A forces c=d=0; hence 1+\eta Z satisfies all defining equations. Its inverse is 1-\eta Z, so it is an element of G(k[\eta]/(\eta^2)).

lean.statement: theorem mixedCommutator_tangent {k n : Type u} {V : Type v} [Field k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [FiniteDimensional k V] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (b : Module.Basis n k V) (G : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] (i : G ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.GeneralLinearGroup n k) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme i] (X Y : Module.End k V) (x y : AlgebraicGeometry.points G (DualNumber k)) (hx : homMulEquiv n k (DualNumber k) (x ≫ i) = dualUnit (LinearMap.toMatrix b b X)) (hy : homMulEquiv n k (DualNumber k) (y ≫ i) = dualUnit (LinearMap.toMatrix b b Y)) : ∃ p q : AlgebraicGeometry.points G (DualNumber (DualNumber k)), homMulEquiv n k (DualNumber (DualNumber k)) (p ≫ i) = Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map (inlHom (DualNumber k) (DualNumber k)) (dualUnit (LinearMap.toMatrix b b X)) ∧ homMulEquiv n k (DualNumber (DualNumber k)) (q ≫ i) = Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map (DualNumber.mapRingHom (inlHom k k)) (dualUnit (LinearMap.toMatrix b b Y)) ∧ (homMulEquiv n k (DualNumber (DualNumber k)) ((p * q * p⁻¹ * q⁻¹) ≫ i) : Matrix n n (DualNumber (DualNumber k))) = (1 + (LinearMap.toMatrix b b X).map (fun a ↦ inl (inr a))) * (1 + (LinearMap.toMatrix b b Y).map (fun a ↦ inr (inl a))) * (1 - (LinearMap.toMatrix b b X).map (fun a ↦ inl (inr a))) * (1 - (LinearMap.toMatrix b b Y).map (fun a ↦ inr (inl a))) ∧ (homMulEquiv n k (DualNumber (DualNumber k)) ((p * q * p⁻¹ * q⁻¹) ≫ i) : Matrix n n (DualNumber (DualNumber k))) = 1 + (LinearMap.toMatrix b b (X * Y - Y * X)).map (fun a ↦ inr (inr a)) ∧ Function.Injective (DualNumber.mulRingHom (R := k)) ∧ ∃ z : AlgebraicGeometry.points G (DualNumber k), homMulEquiv n k (DualNumber k) (z ≫ i) = dualUnit (LinearMap.toMatrix b b (X * Y - Y * X))
